validated_work_order.confidence_rationale: Reproduced end-to-end in the running app by driving the reporter's steps myself, and the mechanism confirmed independently at the SQL layer with a throwaway vitest in the loot-core AQL harness ($sumOver under date asc returns 75/-25/25 where 100/50/75 is correct). The candidate fix was also executed at the SQL layer: rebuilding the query with orderExpressions replaced by [{date:'desc'}] restores the correct 75/50/100 regardless of the user's sort. What holds it below 100: I did not observe state.balances through the React tree, so the Account.tsx -> visibleColumns link rests on DOM observation (header and cells vanish) plus code reading rather than direct state inspection; and whether the helper should live in a new file or inline is left to the implementer.
validated_work_order.understanding: Reported: on the desktop register, enabling the running-balance column works, sorting Date descending shows correct balances, but a second Date click (ascending) makes the whole Balance column disappear and removes the Balance toggle from 'Manage table columns', so it cannot be turned back on without first changing the sort. Reproduced myself in the running app at $PREVIEW_URL against the demo budget, on a single real account (Capital One Checking), using the reporter's steps in order. Observed: with the Balance column enabled, one Date click gave header 'Date|Payee|Notes|Category|Payment|Deposit|Balance|check' with 24 balance cells and first row 10/02/2026; the second Date click gave header 'Date|Payee|Notes|Category|Payment|Deposit|check' with 0 balance cells and first row 08/01/2026 (oldest first, so the sort genuinely flipped to asc, not a stale render). A third Date click (back to desc) restored the column and 24 balance cells. Opening 'Manage table columns' while descending listed a balance toggle; opening the same modal while ascending listed no balance entry at all (#toggle-column-balance count 0). So the loss of the column and the loss of the toggle are one condition, and the condition is exactly 'sort is date/asc' - not search, not filters, not the account being a pseudo-view. I separately confirmed the neighbouring guards still work and must be preserved: sorting by Payee gives 0 balance cells and no modal toggle; under date/desc a search term drops the column to 0 cells and clearing it restores 24.
validated_work_order.root_cause: Account.tsx `canCalculateBalance()` returns true only when the sort is absent, or is `field === 'date' && ascDesc === 'desc'`. It is a direction gate, not a data gate: when it returns false, (a) `calculateBalances()` short-circuits and returns `null`, so `this.state.balances` is set to `null` by the `onData` handler; (b) `render()` passes `showBalances={!!allBalances}`, and `allBalances` is that same `null`, so `showBalances` is false; (c) `visibleColumns` in TransactionsTable then filters the 'balance' column out of the render list, removing the header cell and every row cell; and (d) `onManageColumns()` filters the 'balance' column out of the columns passed to the modal, which is why the toggle vanishes. The gate exists because the balance query uses `$sumOver`, which compiles to `SUM(amount) OVER (ORDER BY <the query's own orderExpressions> ROWS BETWEEN CURRENT ROW AND UNBOUNDED FOLLOWING)`. `calculateBalances()` passes `this.paged.query`, which already carries the user's display sort. The window frame always runs CURRENT ROW -> UNBOUNDED FOLLOWING, so it only yields a correct running balance when the ordering runs newest-to-oldest. Under date/asc the same window sums each row forward toward newer transactions and returns wrong numbers, so the guard suppresses the column rather than showing them. The bug is that the correct answer was made unreachable instead of computed: the balance per transaction is a property of the transaction, not of the display order, and the display sort is only being used as the window's frame.
evidence:
Reproduction driven with Playwright against $PREVIEW_URL=http://localhost:3001 (Vite dev server, demo budget loaded via 'Try the demo', single account 'Capital One Checking'). Command: `node ./.sdlc-repro.mjs` run from the repo root (scratch script, deleted afterwards; `git status` clean apart from untracked plan/). Output:

  [after-enable] header="10/02/2026 Home Depot #home-improvement Food 42.20 1,432.61"  balanceCells=24
  [desc]         header="10/02/2026 Home Depot #home-improvement Food 42.20 1,432.61"  balanceCells=24
  [MODAL-desc]   balanceToggleCount=1
  [asc]          header="08/15/2026 Starting Balance Starting Balances 1,003.95"          balanceCells=0
  [asc] row1     firstDate=08/01/2026
  [MODAL-asc]    balanceToggleCount=0
  [desc-again]   header="10/02/2026 ..."  balanceCells=24

  firstDate moving 10/02/2026 -> 08/01/2026 confirms the sort really flipped to ascending, so the column loss is not a stale-render artifact; the third click restoring the column confirms desc is the only direction affected.

  No console errors and no network responses >= 400 accompanied the failure (the only console line was an unrelated OPFS persistence warning). The column is removed by a render-time filter, not by an exception, which is why it fails silently.

Neighbouring guards confirmed still working, so the fix must preserve them: sorting by Payee (non-date field) gives balanceCells=0 and modal balanceToggleCount=0; under date/desc, typing into the Search box gives balanceCells=0 and clearing it restores balanceCells=24; under date/asc the column is already absent and stays absent with search applied. Command: `node ./.sdlc-probe2.mjs` (scratch, deleted).

Mechanism confirmed independently at the SQL layer. A throwaway test in packages/loot-core (aql/exec.test.ts harness style: one account, three transactions dated 2024-01-01/02/03 with amounts 100/-50/25, so correct running balances are 100/50/75) selecting `[{ balance: { $sumOver: '$amount' } }]` gave:

  DESC  (orderBy {date:'desc'}) -> [{balance:75,id:t3},{balance:50,id:t2},{balance:100,id:t1}]   correct
  ASC   (orderBy {date:'asc'})  -> [{balance:75,id:t1},{balance:-25,id:t2},{balance:25,id:t3}]  wrong
  FIXED (same query, orderExpressions replaced by [{date:'desc'}]) -> [{balance:75,id:t3},{balance:50,id:t2},{balance:100,id:t1}]  correct

  Command: `cd packages/loot-core && ENV=node npx vitest --run src/server/aql/scratch-probe.test.ts` (scratch file deleted afterwards).

  The FIXED row is the decisive one: it is the same filters and the same select, differing only in the window's orderExpressions, so making the window order-independent is sufficient and does not require changing `$sumOver`.

Which tests CI actually collects was checked directly, because the previous plan's acceptance criteria leaned on it. `packages/desktop-client/vite.config.mts:406` sets `test.include: ['src/**/*.{test,spec}.?(c|m)[jt]s?(x)']`, and `packages/desktop-client/package.json` defines `"test": "vitest --run"`, which root `yarn test` (lage test --continue) runs - so anything under `e2e/` is never collected. Confirmed by running `cd packages/desktop-client && npx vitest --run src/components/accounts/Balance.test.tsx`, which was collected and passed, while no e2e file is reachable from that include. `.sdlc/config.yml` has `verify.e2e: ""`, and `.github/workflows/ci-verify.yml` skips the e2e step when that is empty, so no CI check runs the Playwright suite. Consequence: an AC may not lean on an e2e file for CI proof. AC-2 and AC-4 have been changed from `verify: "test"` to `verify: "browser"` accordingly, and a CI-collected unit test has been added under `src/components/accounts/`.
validated_work_order.approach:
Make the running balance independent of the display sort direction, then drop the direction clause from `canCalculateBalance()` so the column and its toggle survive an ascending sort.

In `Account.tsx`, build the balance query so its window ordering is always newest-to-oldest, independent of `this.paged.query`'s user sort. Concretely: take the paged query's serialized state, replace `orderExpressions` wholesale with an explicit `[{ date: 'desc' }, { sort_order: 'desc' }]` (the second entry mirrors the tiebreaker `applySort` appends, so equal-date rows stay deterministic), and keep everything else - filters, `options({ splits: 'none' })`, table - untouched. `Query.orderBy` APPENDS to `orderExpressions` rather than replacing them, so the user's sort must be dropped, not appended after; a `new Query({ ...state, orderExpressions })` rebuild is the form verified to work. Note `Account.tsx` currently imports `Query` as a type only (line 20); constructing one needs the value import.

Then relax `canCalculateBalance()` from `sort.field === 'date' && sort.ascDesc === 'desc'` to accept a date sort in either direction. Keep returning false for a non-date sort field, a non-empty `search`, and non-empty `filterConditions` - those genuinely make a running balance meaningless, because a filtered set does not accumulate to the account total. Both were confirmed working today and must survive.

Once the guard no longer excludes ascending, all three consumers follow from the one change: `state.balances` stops being nulled, `showBalances={!!allBalances}` stays true so `visibleColumns` keeps the column, and `onManageColumns()` keeps passing the balance column to the modal so the toggle stays available. `grep` confirms exactly three callers of the guard, all in this file: the reconciled-rows filter, `calculateBalances()`, and `onManageColumns()`.

Put the query construction in a small exported pure helper in its own file under `packages/desktop-client/src/components/accounts/` (e.g. `balanceQuery.ts`), so it can be unit-tested. This is not cosmetic: `vite.config.mts` collects only `src/**`, so a test placed next to the helper is the only regression test CI actually runs for this change. The e2e cases stay in `tests[]` regardless - they are the right regression test for a human running the suite.

Prefer this over simply deleting the guard: deleting it alone would render the Balance column with the wrong numbers the AQL probe above produced (75/-25/25), trading a missing column for a silently wrong one. The values must stay correct under ascending display, not merely present.

Do not change `$sumOver` in compiler.ts. The CURRENT ROW -> UNBOUNDED FOLLOWING frame is a correct, general window; the bug is that a display sort is allowed to define it. `calculateRunningBalancesTopDown` in `hooks/useTransactions.ts` is the mobile equivalent and already handles ascending; it is a separate client-side path and is out of scope.

files.change: New module exporting the balance-window query construction as a pure function: take a `Query` (the paged transactions query) and return a new `Query` whose `orderExpressions` are `[{ date: 'desc' }, { sort_order: 'desc' }]`, with every other part of the serialized state (filters, tableOptions/splits, table) carried over unchanged. Implement the replacement by constructing `new Query({ ...query.serialize(), orderExpressions: [...] })` from `@actual-app/core/shared/query` - NOT by calling `.orderBy(...)`, which appends and would leave the user's ascending sort in front of the new one. Keep it free of React and of any dependency on `Account.tsx` state so it is unit-testable on its own.
files.why: Two reasons. Mechanically, it is the change that makes the running balance correct under an ascending display sort. Structurally, `vite.config.mts` collects only `src/**`, so a test beside this file is the only regression test CI runs for this change - an e2e test is never collected.

files.change: In `calculateBalances()`, replace `this.paged.query.options({ splits: 'none' }).select([{ balance: { $sumOver: '$amount' } }])` with the same chain applied to the query returned by the new `balanceQuery.ts` helper, so the `$sumOver` window's ordering is always newest-to-oldest regardless of the user's display sort. `Account.tsx` imports `Query` as a type only at line 20; if the helper is called from here rather than imported wholesale, a value import is needed. In `canCalculateBalance()`, replace the clause `this.state.sort.field === 'date' && this.state.sort.ascDesc === 'desc'` with an acceptance of a date sort in either direction, so an ascending sort no longer returns false. Keep returning false for a non-date sort field, a non-empty `search`, and non-empty `filterConditions` - all three were confirmed working today and must not regress.
files.why: Both halves of the reported symptom trace to this one guard: it nulls `state.balances`, which makes `showBalances` false and drops the column in TransactionsTable's `visibleColumns`, and it also removes the column from the list passed to 'Manage table columns'. The guard is direction-based because the balance window currently inherits the user's sort; making the window order-independent is what removes the need for the direction clause.

cases: FAILS BEFORE THE FIX, PASSES AFTER: given a query carrying the user's ascending display sort (`q('transactions').filter({account:'acct'}).orderBy({date:'asc'})`), the balance query the helper returns has `orderExpressions` exactly `[{date:'desc'}, {sort_order:'desc'}]` - no `{date:'asc'}` anywhere in it. Before the fix the window inherits the ascending sort (measured in the live app: the column vanishes; measured at the SQL layer: 75/-25/25 instead of 100/50/75), so this assertion is the CI-collected regression test for the defect.

Rebuilding preserves every filter: the helper's output carries the same `filterExpressions` as its input, so the account filter and the reconciled-rows filter added at Account.tsx:483-488 survive and the balances are not computed over a wider row set than the table shows.

A query that already has no orderExpressions gains the explicit newest-first ordering rather than being left unordered, so the balance window is deterministic on first load before any sort is applied.
A query already ordered `{date:'desc'}` round-trips unchanged, pinning that the fix is a no-op for the currently-working direction and cannot regress it.

Running balance column stays visible when the Date column is sorted oldest-first: enable the Balance column, click Date once (descending) and assert the header contains 'Balance' and at least one row has a `data-testid="balance"` cell, then click Date again (ascending) and assert the header STILL contains 'Balance' and the row count with a non-empty balance cell equals the total row count.

Running balance values are correct under an ascending sort: with three known transactions (oldest to newest, amounts 100, -50, 25) sorted oldest-first, assert the rendered balance cells read 100, 50, 75 in that row order - the same values the descending view shows for the same transactions. This is the case that fails today and must not be traded for a merely-present-but-wrong column.

The Balance column remains toggleable while sorted oldest-first: with an ascending Date sort active, open 'Manage table columns' and assert `#toggle-column-balance` exists (today its count is 0), and that unchecking then rechecking it still works.
Sorting back to descending after an ascending sort leaves the balance column and its values intact (no stale or cleared balances on the round trip).

The preserved restrictions still hold: sorting by the Payee column suppresses the balance cells and removes `#toggle-column-balance` from the modal, and under date/desc an active search suppresses the balance cells while clearing the search restores them.

Document the window semantics the fix relies on: `select([{ balance: { $sumOver: '$amount' } }])` over transactions ordered `date desc` yields the correct running balances (75/50/100 for amounts 100/-50/25 dated oldest-to-newest), and the same query ordered `date asc` does NOT (it yields 75/-25/25). Stated plainly: this case PASSES BEFORE AND AFTER the change - it pins that `CURRENT ROW -> UNBOUNDED FOLLOWING` is only a running balance for a newest-first ordering, so a future change to `$sumOver` or to this query cannot quietly alter it. It is not the regression test; the regression test is the `src/components/accounts/balanceQuery.test.ts` case above.

qa_script: 1. Start the app and open the demo budget ('Try the demo'), then open a real single account from the sidebar (e.g. 'Capital One Checking'). Do NOT use /accounts/onbudget or another pseudo-account - the balance column is unavailable there for an unrelated reason (see out_of_scope).
2. Note the header row and the first row's date. Record the first and last dates so you can tell the sort direction apart.
3. Account menu -> 'Manage table columns' -> tick 'Balance' -> Save. Confirm the header now contains 'Balance' and rows show balance values.

4. Click the Date column header once. Confirm the first row is the newest transaction, the Balance column is still present, and balances look correct (the top row's balance should equal the account's current balance).

5. Click the Date header again. THIS IS THE FAILING STEP on current code. Confirm the first row is now the OLDEST transaction. Assert the header STILL contains 'Balance' and every row still shows a balance value.

6. Cross-check the numbers: for the same three transactions, the balance shown next to a given transaction must be the same whether the list is sorted oldest-first or newest-first (e.g. amounts 100, -50, 25 dated oldest-to-newest must read 100, 50, 75 in both directions). A column that is present but showing different or nonsensical numbers is still a failure.

7. While still sorted oldest-first, open 'Account menu' -> 'Manage table columns'. Confirm 'Balance' is still listed and its toggle works (uncheck, Save, reopen, check, Save) without changing the sort first.
8. Click the Date header a third time to return to newest-first. Confirm the Balance column and its correct values come back.

9. Negative check, in turn: sort by the Payee column, then apply a search, then apply a filter. Each must suppress the Balance column (existing behaviour that must not regress), and clearing the search must restore it.

10. Regression: run `yarn typecheck` and `yarn lint`, plus `yarn test` (lage). Note that `yarn test` does NOT run the Playwright e2e suite in this repository (`vite.config.mts` collects only `src/**`), so the e2e cases in this change are for a human running the suite, not a CI gate - the CI-collected regression test is `packages/desktop-client/src/components/accounts/balanceQuery.test.ts`.
risks: The most likely wrong fix is deleting the ascDesc guard without making the window order-independent. That turns a missing column into a silently WRONG column: the AQL probe measured date-asc returning 75/-25/25 instead of 100/50/75. AC-2 exists specifically to catch that, and reviewers should treat a diff that only touches `canCalculateBalance()` as incomplete.

The balance query is built from `this.paged.query`, which also carries any active filters and the reconciled-rows filter applied at Account.tsx:483-488. Replacing `orderExpressions` must not also drop `filterExpressions`, or the balances will be computed over a different row set than the table shows. A unit test asserts the filters survive.

`Query.orderBy` appends to `orderExpressions` rather than replacing them, so naively appending `{ date: 'desc' }` to the existing query would leave the user's ascending sort in front of it and silently change nothing - the bug would appear unfixed. The helper must replace the array wholesale.

`onSaveColumns` (Account.tsx:988-1005) has a side effect when the balance column is re-enabled: it clears `transactions`, `filterConditions`, `search`, and `sort`, then refetches. If the modal now offers the balance toggle in states where it previously did not, this reset will fire in more situations. Verify it does not silently discard a user's search or filter without the UI saying so.

The account page also uses `canCalculateBalance()` for the reconciled-rows filter (Account.tsx:483-488). Relaxing the guard changes which rows are loaded when reconciled transactions are hidden - correct in principle (it matches what date/desc already does), but it is a second behavioural effect of the same change and should be checked, not assumed. AC-5 exercises the round trip.

Making the balance column appear under conditions where it previously did not means more users will hit the balance query path; it is a `$sumOver` window over the account's transactions, so its cost on very large accounts should be sanity-checked.

This repository is an imported snapshot (a single 'Import actualbudget/actual' commit), so `git log -S` / `git blame` on `canCalculateBalance` yields no history and cannot say when the guard was introduced or why. The intent behind the direction check is inferred from the `$sumOver` frame semantics and the AQL probe, not from a commit message. An implementer with upstream history available should sanity-check that inference.

alternatives_considered.approach: Just delete the sort-direction clause from `canCalculateBalance()` so the column always shows.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: The column would render with wrong numbers. `$sumOver` compiles to `SUM(amount) OVER (ORDER BY <query orders> ROWS BETWEEN CURRENT ROW AND UNBOUNDED FOLLOWING)` and the frame direction is fixed, so under date/asc it sums forward toward newer rows. Measured at the SQL layer: 75/-25/25 where 100/50/75 is correct. Replaces a visible bug with a silent data bug.

alternatives_considered.approach: Compute the running balance client-side in JS (as the mobile path does with `calculateRunningBalancesTopDown` in hooks/useTransactions.ts) instead of via the `$sumOver` window.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: Works, but it discards the database-side window that exists precisely to avoid loading and accumulating the whole transaction set in the browser, and it forks the desktop and mobile balance logic into two implementations. The smaller, more faithful fix is to keep the window and stop letting a display sort define its ordering.

alternatives_considered.approach: Extend `$sumOver` in packages/loot-core/src/server/aql/compiler.ts to accept an explicit frame (e.g. UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) so ascending orderings work without changing the query.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: Changes a general, correct, shared AQL primitive to serve one caller's display state. `CURRENT ROW AND UNBOUNDED FOLLOWING` is not wrong; it is just the wrong frame for an ascending display order. Widening the AQL surface is a bigger blast radius than fixing the query that builds the window.

alternatives_considered.approach: Keep the guard and instead make the UI reset the sort (or refuse to sort ascending) when the balance column is on.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: Fights the user: it removes a sort the table advertises as available and diverges from the mobile view, which already supports running balances in both directions. The data supports both orderings; only the query construction was direction-bound.

alternatives_considered.approach: Keep every regression case under `e2e/` only, with no unit test, on the grounds that the Playwright test is the most faithful reproduction.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: No CI check in this repository runs the e2e suite: `.sdlc/config.yml` has `verify.e2e: ""` (so ci-verify.yml's e2e step exits 0 vacuously), and `packages/desktop-client/vite.config.mts` collects only `src/**`, so `yarn test` never reaches `e2e/`. A plan whose regression coverage lives only there is green on a full revert of the change. Hence the helper in `src/components/accounts/` with a co-located vitest case, with the e2e cases kept alongside it.

out_of_scope: Pseudo-account views (`/accounts/onbudget`, `/accounts/offbudget`, `/accounts/uncategorized`): `canCalculateBalance()` returns false there because `accounts.find(a => a.id === accountId)` matches nothing for these ids, so the Balance column is filtered out of the modal and cannot be enabled at all. Same guard, different trigger, separate fix - it needs a decision about what a running balance means across a set of accounts, not just an ordering change.

`calculateRunningBalancesTopDown` (hooks/useTransactions.ts:219-259), the mobile equivalent. Its index arithmetic looks independently questionable (index 0 sets `startingBalance`, the last index sets the bare `transaction.amount`, everything between subtracts the previous amount), but mobile running balances were not part of the reproduction and were not exercised here.

Setting `verify.e2e` in `.sdlc/config.yml` so CI would run the Playwright suite. That file is in `forbidden_paths`, so it is not available as a way to give the e2e cases CI coverage. AC-2 and AC-4 were therefore marked `verify: "browser"` rather than `verify: "test"`, with the browser steps spelled out in `how_to_verify`.
assumptions: The desktop register's 'Manage table columns' modal is the feature the reporter called the hamburger menu / 'show running balance' toggle - in this codebase version the running balance is a Balance column toggled there, not a separate menu item. The reproduction confirms that modal is where the toggle lives.
`calculateBalances()` is the only producer of `state.balances` on this page, so fixing its ordering fixes every consumer without touching `TransactionsTable`.
unknowns: Whether upstream fixed this differently - the repository is a squashed import with no usable history, and issue 3808 is still open upstream as of the report.

residual_risks: CI does not run the Playwright suite in this repository, so the end-to-end reproduction lives in `e2e/accounts.test.ts` and is exercised only when a human runs it. The CI-collected regression test (`src/components/accounts/balanceQuery.test.ts`) covers the query construction - the actual defect - but not the render path that drops the column; AC-1, AC-3 and AC-4 are browser checks that depend on QA running them.

The query-construction unit test asserts the shape of the balance query, not the balance numbers a user sees. If a future change altered `$sumOver` itself, that test would still pass; the `loot-core` AQL case added alongside it is what pins the window semantics.
